newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: DAVID HANNAH TO BE LAST ENTRANT UP THE DERWENT
The final boat to finish the Sydney to Hobart yacht race is expected to tie up in Hobart around lunchtime today.
David Hannah from the Port Adelaide Sailing Club is approaching the Derwent River.
Meanwhile, the final handicap placings for the race have been announced.
Alice Springs yacht, Neata Glass, has won Division F.
NATIONAL PARTY DEVELOPING OPTIONS ON A REPUBLIC
Ahead of a March conference on the Republic issue, the National Party says its considering a range of options should the Australian people choose a republic.
Party leader, Tim Fischer says among the options is a plan which requires the Chief Justice of the High Court to assume the Queen's constitutional role.
Mr Fischer says the "minimalist" model would empower the Chief Justice to appoint or dismiss the Governor General.
He says the discussion of options does not, however, mean that his party is coming around to the idea of a Republic.
The deputy Prime Minister says Australia's existing constitution has served this country well, and shouldn't be tampered with on a whim.
MAN TO BE CHARGED OVER GATE-CRASHING GOVERNMENT HOUSE
Police in Melbourne say a forced entry into the grounds of Government House overnight was not politically motivated.
They are expected to charge a man this morning, after he allegedly rammed his vehicle through the entrance gates, causing 15 thousand dollars damage.
Security staff claim the man, aged in his twenties, drove several hundred metres into the grounds and past the governors residence before being apprehended.
The governor was not at home at the time of the incident.
CENTURY "COULD KICK-START MINING INVESTMENT"
The Queensland Mining Council says the fate of the Century Zinc project in north-west Queensland during 1997 could hold the key to future mining investment in Australia.
Council Chief Executive, Michael Pinnock, says a decision on the mine will shape the industry's year, particularly if the project gets the go-ahead.
Mr Pinnock says if there's a favourable outcome, it will show there's a way to resolve native title issues.
But he says if the mine fails, it will cast a pall over the entire metalliferous sector in the coming year.
He says the mine would create an enormous boom, not only for Queensland, but for all of Australia.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373 1800
